dedupe_keys.name: co adoption of low carbon household energy technologies agent based model of pv ev heat pump and home battery diffusion romandie switzerland

description: This agent-based model simulates how households adopt four low-carbon technologies, rooftop solar panels, electric vehicles, heat pumps and home batteries, and in particular how they adopt them together. The CoMSES Net release read on 2026-09-28 (version 1.0.1, published 23 February 2024 by van der Kam, Lagomarsino, Azar, Hahnel and Parra) explains that each agent decides whether to adopt each technology, with decisions grounded in the risks-as-feelings model and environmental and social psychology, and that agent behaviour is informed by survey data from 1,469 people in the French-speaking Swiss region of Romandie. The combination matters because electric vehicles, heat pumps and batteries offer flexible demand and storage that can ease the grid integration of solar power. It is written in NetLogo. Access is free download under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the survey calibration is regional, and grid effects are not simulated inside the model. It supports capacity planning of distribution grids by giving adoption scenarios for distributed resources. No related household technology diffusion model is catalogued.
name: Co-adoption of low-carbon household energy technologies: agent-based model of PV, EV, heat pump and home battery diffusion (Romandie, Switzerland)
outputs: adoption and co-adoption paths of PV, EVs, heat pumps and batteries
provider: Mart van der Kam, Maria Lagomarsino, Elie Azar, Ulf Hahnel and David Parra (CoMSES Net)

sources.note: read (CoMSES JSON): version 1.0.1 published 23 February 2024, CC-BY-4.0, NetLogo, 150 downloads; simulates household diffusion of PV panels, EVs, heat pumps and home batteries and their co-adoption; decisions grounded on risks-as-feelings model and environmental psychology; agent behaviour informed by survey data among 1,469 people in the Swiss region Romandie; used to build diffusion scenarios and as a virtual experimentation environment

title_en: Co-adoption of low-carbon household energy technologies: agent-based model of PV, EV, heat pump and home battery diffusion (Romandie, Switzerland)
